life_summary: John E. Page was born in 1799 in the northeastern United States during a period of religious ferment and revival. Little is definitively documented about his early life and secular pursuits prior to joining the Latter-day Saint movement. Page came of age during an era of westward expansion and participated in various settlement efforts. He was married multiple times as polygamy became doctrine within the church. Page worked as a lay preacher and missionary, traveling extensively to spread the gospel message. His life was marked by the tumultuous events of early church history, including conflicts in Missouri and Illinois.
church_summary: Page was an early convert to the LDS Church and served as an apostle, though records of his exact tenure and contributions are less detailed than those of some of his contemporaries. He participated in various missionary missions and was involved in church settlement projects. Page's ministry took place during the foundational era of the church when institutional structures were still being developed and major theological doctrines were being established. He remained involved in church activities throughout the early period of Latter-day Saint history, though documentation of specific callings and accomplishments is limited in readily available sources.
